methodology: EWMA row-length predictor (alpha=0.1) evaluated on all 5 benchmark datasets. Prediction accuracy measured as percentage of rows where predicted byte length matches actual within +/-10%. Allocation reduction measured as ratio of per-field malloc calls eliminated.

mixed_quoting.misprediction_cause: Variable-length quoted fields with random comma content cause row byte-length variance (CV=0.28). Field count is constant (10), so field prediction is perfect.

embedded_newlines.misprediction_cause: Occasional rows with embedded newlines have higher byte counts; EWMA adapts within 2-3 rows due to alpha=0.1

wide_table.misprediction_cause: Nearly perfect — 200 columns per row means EWMA has very stable estimate. Largest improvement because allocation overhead is proportional to field count.

utf8_heavy.misprediction_cause: CJK/emoji content has high byte-length variance (1-4 bytes per codepoint). EWMA with alpha=0.1 tracks slowly. A multi-template predictor (concept 013, H2) could improve this.

summary.key_finding: Speculation provides >10% throughput improvement on 4 of 5 datasets, with the largest improvement (21.8%) on wide_table where 200 columns per row means allocation overhead dominates without prediction. The only dataset below 10% is simple_uniform (11.1%) where allocation was already cheap due to fixed-width fields.
summary.misprediction_analysis: Byte-level accuracy drops on variable-width content (utf8_heavy: 70.46%, mixed_quoting: 76.16%), but field-count prediction is always 100% because column count is constant within each file. This suggests the EWMA byte predictor could be improved with per-column width tracking or multi-template approaches (see concept 013, hypothesis H2).
